parts: For decades, factory robots have worked behind a fence.
People on one side. Machines on the other.
This week, South Korea cleared twenty humanoid robots to work beside people.
The old safety rules assumed robots that stay in one place.
Data from the trial is meant to help rewrite those rules.
The caveat: this is permission to test, not proof that they work.
What matters is how often a person has to step in.
The lesson for builders: trust is earned in small, measured trials.
That's how the fence comes down.
